projection.growthBasis: Epoch AI's February 2026 trend scenario projects USD 770 billion of 2026 capital expenditure across Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle. It extrapolates the quarterly trend since Q2 2023 and is not a realised annual total or current company guidance. The measure includes cash purchases of property, plant and equipment plus new finance leases across all business activities; the AI-specific share is not disclosed. Historical totals sum Epoch's published calendar-quarter data (Oracle quarters are mapped to the calendar quarter with greatest overlap). The growthFactor is the ratio of the displayed 2026 scenario to the 2025 historical total, not a separately estimated growth rate. AI examples below describe individual achievements from their cited years, not returns caused by this projected expenditure.

source: Epoch AI — Hyperscaler capex trend scenario (published February 2026)

sources.name: Brookings — The Telecommunications Crash: What To Do Now?

categories.methodology: Brookings reported more than USD 500 billion invested in fibre, switches and wireless networks during the five years after the 1996 US Telecommunications Act. USD 500 billion is a rounded lower-bound historical benchmark in nominal 1996–2001 dollars, without inflation adjustment. The displayed ratio compares monetary scale only; it is not the cost of rebuilding those networks today.

sources.name: The Planetary Society — How much did the Apollo program cost?

categories.methodology: The Planetary Society's reconstruction of NASA budget records reports USD 25.8 billion for Project Apollo, 1960–1973, or approximately USD 309 billion in 2025 dollars using NASA's New Start Index. This excludes Gemini and robotic lunar programmes, whose inclusion would bring the broader lunar effort to USD 338 billion. It is a historical programme-cost comparison, not a present-day mission quote.

aiBenefit.text: The AlphaFold database paper for 2024 documented over 214 million predicted protein structures, freely accessible to researchers. These are computational predictions with varying confidence, not 214 million experimentally verified structures.

sources.name: AlphaFold Protein Structure Database in 2024 — Nucleic Acids Research
Brookings Institution — The Costs of the Manhattan Project (Atomic Audit, Stephen I. Schwartz)
US Bureau of Labor Statistics — Historical CPI-U, December 2024

categories.methodology: Brookings' Atomic Audit reports cumulative Manhattan Project costs through December 1945 of USD 1,889,604,000 nominal, equivalent to USD 21,570,821,000 in its constant-1996-dollar series. Updating that published 1996-dollar figure with BLS annual-average CPI-U (156.9 in 1996; 313.689 in 2024) gives USD 43.126 billion, rounded here to USD 43.1 billion in 2024 dollars. This is an explicit CPI update of the source's adjusted estimate, not a reconstruction of each wartime expenditure or a current programme quote.

aiBenefit.text: DeepMind and EPFL demonstrated reinforcement-learning control of plasma shapes in the TCV research tokamak in 2022. This was an advance in experimental plasma control, not a demonstration of commercial fusion power.

sources.name: Magnetic control of tokamak plasmas through deep reinforcement learning — Nature
Ceres2030 — Sustainable Solutions to End Hunger, Summary Report

categories.methodology: Ceres2030's 2020 model estimated average additional public spending of USD 33 billion per year through 2030: USD 14 billion from donors plus USD 19 billion from low- and middle-income governments. The scenario combines reducing hunger, doubling small-producer incomes and limiting agricultural emissions; it assumes coordinated interventions and induced private investment. This is a historical model benchmark, not a current funding quote or a guarantee that money alone ends hunger.

aiBenefit.text: WFP reported in April 2026 that HungerMap Live covers more than 50 countries, with AI-assisted forecasts for 16 designated Hunger Hotspots. Forecast coverage is narrower than overall platform coverage.

sources.name: World Bank — The Costs of Meeting the 2030 SDG Targets on Drinking Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene, Summary Report

categories.methodology: World Bank 2016 baseline estimate of USD 37.6 billion per year in 2015 prices for capital investment to extend safely managed drinking-water services to unserved populations in 140 countries during 2015–2030. This is the drinking-water component only; it excludes the additional ongoing operating and maintenance budget and is not an updated 2026 estimate.

aiBenefit.text: In May 2026, Thames Water announced AI-assisted satellite leak detection targeting savings of 100 million litres a day. This is an expected project outcome, not an independently verified realised saving.

sources.name: Thames Water — Leak-detection contract with Origin Tech
WHO — Global Technical Strategy for Malaria 2016–2030, 2021 update
WHO Africa — Bridging the funding gap to defeat malaria in Africa

categories.methodology: WHO's 2021 Global Technical Strategy estimated USD 10.3 billion of annual funding for malaria prevention, diagnosis, treatment and programme delivery by 2030. This is the total annual funding target, not the additional funding gap or the cost of global eradication. It excludes the separate estimated USD 0.85 billion per year for research and development. The strategy targets at least a 90% reduction in incidence and mortality by 2030, not eradication by 2050.

aiBenefit.text: AI-assisted drug discovery produced rentosertib, which was tested in a 71-person Phase 2a lung-fibrosis trial reported in 2025. Larger, longer studies are needed to assess benefits and risks; this is not a malaria treatment.

sources.name: Xu et al. — A generative AI-discovered TNIK inhibitor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: a randomized phase 2a trial, Nature Medicine
Princeton — Net-Zero America Final Report Summary (2021)

categories.methodology: Princeton's 2021 Net-Zero America final summary, page 75, estimates USD 310 billion in additional electricity-transmission capital invested or committed during 2021–2030 in the high-electrification E+ pathway relative to the reference case, in 2018 dollars. The source rounds to the nearest USD 10 billion and includes capital committed to projects entering service after 2030. This is a modelled decade of transmission investment, not an annual cost or a complete grid-modernisation budget.

aiBenefit.text: DeepMind reported in 2016 that its system reduced cooling energy at a Google data centre by up to 40%. The result concerns cooling, not a 40% reduction in total electricity use or a measured improvement across the power grid.

sources.name: DeepMind blog — Reduces Google Data Centre Cooling Bill by 40%
